entities.summary: Pomponius Mela was a Roman geographer born in Tingentera, Spain, around 20 BC, who wrote one of the earliest surviving Roman geographies, the 'De situ orbis', around 43 AD. This work provided detailed information on the geography of the Roman world, including the Mediterranean region and the Black Sea. Mela's work was widely used by Roman authors, including Pliny the Elder, and has been influential in the development of Western geography. Mela's legacy extends beyond his written works, as he played a key role in shaping Roman attitudes towards geography and the natural world. As a result, his work continues to be studied by historians and scholars today.
